THIS CRL.P IS FILED U/S 439 CR.P.C (U/S 483 BNSS) BY THE ADVOCATE FOR THE PETITIONER PRAYING THAT THIS HONOURABLE COURT MAY BE PLEASED TO ENLARGE THE PETITIONER/ACCUSED NO.8 ON BAIL IN SPL.C (POSCO)
NO.71/2024 ARISING IN CR.NO.53/2021, REGISTERED BY THE RESPONDENT NO.1 POLICE/WOMEN P.S., CHITRADURGA, FOR THE ALLEGED OFFENCES U/

370(A), 366(A), 323, 344, 346, 363 OF IPC, SEC. 4, 6, 17 OF POCSO ACT, SEC. 3,4,5 AND 6 OF IMMORAL TRAFFIC PREVENTION ACT, ON THE FILE OF THE HONBLE SPECIAL 2nd ADDITIONAL DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE, CHITRADURGA IN CRL.MISC.NO.863/2024.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE S VISHWAJITH SHETTY  ORAL ORDER Accused No.8 in SC.No.71/2024 pending before the Court of II Additional District and Sessions Judge and Special Judge, Chitradurga, arising out of Crime No.53/2021 registered by Chitradurga Women Police Station, Chitradurga District for the offences punishable under Sections 468, 149,
370(4), 376(2)(n), 370(A), 366(A), 323, 344, 346, 363 of IPC, Sections 4, 6, 17 of POSCO Act, 2012 and Section 3, 4, 5 of Immoral Traffic Prevention Act, 1966 is before this Court under Section 439 of Cr.PC seeking regular bail.

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned HCGP for respondent No.1.
Respondent No.2 though served, is unrepresented before this Court.

3. FIR in Crime No.53/2021 was registered by Chitradurga Women Police Station, Chitradurga District initially for the offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC, against the petitioner herein on the basis of the first information dated 18.08.2021 received from respondent No.2 who is the mother of the victim girl.

entities.text: Chitradurga Women Police Station, Chitradurga District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the first information dated 18.08.2021 it is stated that daughter of the first informant, aged about 15 years was missing from the house from 09.08.2021 onwards, and efforts made to trace her had failed.
Therefore, first informant had approached the police.

2 victim girl was traced on 12.03.2024.

sentences.text:
She had stated that on 09.08.2021, after she left her house,
she had gone to Bengaluru and thereafter to Mysuru and accused No.1, who found the victim girl in the KSRTC Bus Stand at Mysuru had taken the victim girl along with her on the guise of providing her food and NC: 2024:KHC:45144 shelter, and thereafter, had used her for the business of prostitution, forcibly against the wishes of the victim girl.
4. During the course of investigation of the case petitioner herein was arrested on 06.04.2024 and remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed against 10 accused persons.
Petitioner is arrayed as accused No.8 in the charge sheet.
Bail application filed by the petitioner before the Jurisdictional Sessions Court in Crl.Misc.No.863/2024 was rejected on 06.08.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.
5. Learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that allegation against the petitioner herein and as against accused Nos.3, 5 & 9 are similar.
Accused Nos.3, 5 & 9 have been granted regular bail by this Court.
Petitioner has no other criminal antecedents.
Accordingly, he prays to allow this petition.
Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petition, however, he does not dispute the submission made by the learned Counsel for the petitioner.

7. In the charge sheet, it is alleged that accused Nos.1 & 2 were carrying on the illegal business of prostitution and for the said purpose they were using minor victim girl who was found abundaned in the KSRTC Bus Stand, Mysore by accused No.1.

Allegation against the petitioner who is arrayed as accused No.8 in the charge sheet is that he was arranging for the premises in his locality and also bringing customers to the said premises to have sexual intercourse with the victim girl and thereby he was assisting accused Nos.1 & 2.
Similar allegations are found in the charge sheet even as against accused Nos.3.

Accused No.3 has been granted regular bail by this Court in Crl.P.No.9735/2024 and accused Nos.5 & 9 have been granted regular bail by this Court in Crl.P.No.9315/2024 and Crl.P.No.10618/2024 disposed of on 30.10.2024.
Undisputedly, petitioner who has no criminal antecedents NC: 2024:KHC:45144 is in custody from 06.04.2024.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
Considering the aforesaid aspects of the matter, I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of regular bail needs to be answered affirmatively.

Accordingly, the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is directed to be enlarged on bail in SC.No.71/2024 pending before the Court of II Additional District and Sessions Judge and Special Judge, Chitradurga,
arising out of Crime No.53/2021 registered by Chitradurga Women Police Station,
Chitradurga District for the offences punishable under Sections 468, 149, 370(4),
376(2)(n), 370(A), 366(A), 323, 344, 346, 363 of IPC, Sections 4, 6, 17 of POSCO Act,
2012 and Section 3, 4, 5 of Immoral Traffic Prevention Act, 1966, subject to the following conditions:
Santhosha M vs State Of Karnataka on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155820494/
3 NC: 2024:KHC:45144 a) The petitioner shall execute personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) with two sureties for the likesum, to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court;
b) The petitioner shall appear regularly on all the dates of hearing before the Trial Court unless the Trial Court exempts his appearance for valid reasons;
c) The petitioner shall not directly or indirectly threaten or tamper with the prosecution witnesses;
d) The petitioner shall not involve in similar offences in future;
 e) The petitioner shall not leave the  jurisdiction of the Trial Court without permission of the said Court until the case registered against his is disposed off.
Sd/-
